akhfash:2-2.t: He said ﴿فَأَتَاهُمُ ٱللَّهُ مِنْ حَيْثُ﴾: He means "Allah came to them", i.e. His command came to them. Some read ﴿فَآتاهُم اللهُ﴾, i.e. He brought the punishment to them, because you say "أَتاهُ" (he came to him) and "آتاهُ" (he brought to him), as you say "ذَهَبَ" (he went) and "أَذْهَبَتهُ" (I took him away).

akhfash:5-5.t: And He said ﴿مَا قَطَعْتُمْ مِّن لِّينَةٍ﴾: it is from "اللَّوْنِ" (a kind of palm), as a collective, and its singular is "لِينَة"; it is a kind of palm tree. But since what precedes it took kasra, it (the wāw) turned into yāʾ.

akhfash:6-6.t: And He said ﴿مَآ أَفَآءَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ رَسُولِهِ﴾ because you say: "فَاءَ عَلَيَّ كَذَا وَكَذَا" (such-and-such reverted to me) and "أَفَاءَهُ اللهُ" (Allah made it revert), as you say: "جَاءَ" (he came) and "أَجَاءَهُ اللهُ" (Allah brought him); it is like "ذَهَبَ" and "أَذْهَبْتُهُ".

akhfash:7-7.t: And He said ﴿كَيْ لاَ يَكُونَ دُولَةً﴾: "الدُّوْلَةُ" in this meaning is that the wealth is once for this one and once for that one. You say: "كانَتْ لَنَا عَلَيْهِم الدَوْلَة" (we had the turn of fortune over them). As for its accusative, it is on the basis of "so that the fayʾ (spoils) may not be a thing circulating" (كَيْلاَ يكونَ الفَيْءُ دُوْلَةً), and "كيلا تكون دُوْلَةً", i.e. "so that the booty may not be a thing circulating". [And] they claim that "الدَوْلَة" (with fatḥa) for wealth is also a dialect of the Arabs, but "الدَوْلَة" for wealth is hardly known.

akhfash:9-9.t: And He said ﴿وَلاَ يَجِدُونَ فِي صُدُورِهِمْ حَاجَةً مِّمَّآ أُوتُواْ﴾, i.e. of what they were given.

akhfash:12-12.t:
And He said ﴿لَئِنْ أُخْرِجُواْ لاَ يَخْرُجُونَ مَعَهُمْ﴾: He put the last (verb) in the indicative because it depends on the oath, since this lām at the beginning of the speech is only for the oath, as in the poet's words [in the ṭawīl metre; this is poetic witness no. 270]:
لَئِنْ عادَلِي عبدُ العَزِيزِ بِمِثْلِهَا * وَأَمكَنَنِي مِنْها إِذاً لا أُقِيلُها
(If ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz returns to me with the like of it and gives me power over it, then I will not let it go.)

akhfash:17-17.t: And He said ﴿أَنَّهُمَا فِي ٱلنَّارِ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا﴾: He put "the two abiding" in the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and ﴿فِي ٱلنَّارِ﴾ is the khabar (predicate). Had the speech been "إِنَّهُما في النارِ", the nominative in ﴿خالدَيْنِ﴾ would be allowed. Their saying "when you bring 'فيها' twice it is accusative" is nothing; "فيها" is only emphasis — whether you bring it or not is the same. Do you not see that the Arabs often make it a ḥāl when there is emphasis and the like in it? In the Quran it is accusative in more than one place. He said ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَابِ وَٱلْمُشْرِكِينَ فِي نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ خَالِدِينَ فِيهَآ﴾.

daas-irab:1-1.t: ﴿سَبَّحَ﴾ a past verb. ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) it. ﴿ما﴾ fāʿil (agent). ﴿فِي السَّماواتِ﴾ both attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿وَما فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its two khabars (predicates); the clause is circumstantial (ḥāliyya).

daas-irab:2-2.t: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿أَخْرَجَ﴾ a past verb, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ its object; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of الذين. ﴿مِنْ أَهْلِ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿الْكِتابِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿مِنْ دِيارِهِمْ﴾ both attached to أخرج. ﴿لِأَوَّلِ﴾ both also attached to أخرج. ﴿الْحَشْرِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿ما﴾ negative. ﴿ظَنَنْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿أَنْ يَخْرُجُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by أن, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from أن and the verb stands in place of the two objects of ظننتم, and the clause ظننتم is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَظَنُّوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَنَّهُمْ﴾ anna and its noun (ism). ﴿مانِعَتُهُمْ﴾ its khabar. ﴿حُصُونُهُمْ﴾ the fāʿil of مانعتهم; the interpreted maṣdar from أن and what follows it stands in place of the two objects of ظنوا. ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ both attached to مانعتهم. ﴿فَأَتاهُمُ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb and its object, and the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿مِنْ﴾ a preposition. ﴿حَيْثُ﴾ an adverb (ẓarf), indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, in the position of the genitive; the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to أتاهم. ﴿لَمْ يَحْتَسِبُوا﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿وَقَذَفَ﴾ conjoined to فأتاهم. ﴿فِي قُلُوبِهِمُ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿الرُّعْبَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿يُخْرِبُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بُيُوتَهُمْ﴾ its object. ﴿بِأَيْدِيهِمْ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿وَأَيْدِي﴾ conjoined to أيديهم. ﴿الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿فَاعْتَبِرُوا﴾ the fāʾ is the fāʾ al-faṣīḥa (the fāʾ indicating an implied condition), and an imperative verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the apodosis of the implied condition, with no grammatical position. ﴿يا أُولِي﴾ the one addressed in the vocative (munādā), muḍāf. ﴿الْأَبْصارِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi.

daas-irab:3-3.t: ﴿وَلَوْلا﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and لولا is a non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿أَنْ كَتَبَ اللَّهُ﴾ أن is maṣdariyya (infinitival), and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿عَلَيْهِمُ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿الْجَلاءَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from أن and what follows it is in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted. ﴿لَعَذَّبَهُمْ﴾ the lām occurs in the response (jawāb) of لولا, and عذبهم is a past verb and its object, the fāʿil being latent (mustatir). ﴿فِي الدُّنْيا﴾ both attached to the verb; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position. The wāw is a resumptive particle. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a fronted khabar. ﴿فِي الْآخِرَةِ﴾ both attached to an omitted second khabar. ﴿عَذابُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿النَّارِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:4-4.t: ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿بِأَنَّهُمْ﴾ the bāʾ is a preposition, and anna and its noun (ism). ﴿شَاقُّوا اللَّهَ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of أن, and the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from أن and what follows it is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; and the Name of Majesty is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَرَسُولَهُ﴾ conjoined to الله. ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ a jussive conditional noun, mubtadaʾ. ﴿يُشَاقِّ اللَّهَ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), the fāʿil being latent (mustatir), and the Name of Majesty is mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and inna, its noun and its khabar. ﴿الْعِقابِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clauses of the condition and the apodosis are the khabar of من, and the clause إن is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ).

daas-irab:5-5.t:
﴿ما﴾ a jussive conditional noun, a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿قَطَعْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿مِنْ لِينَةٍ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿تَرَكْتُمُوها﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its first object. ﴿قائِمَةً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿عَلى أُصُولِها﴾ both attached to قائمة. ﴿فَبِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and بإذن: both attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "so cutting it is by the permission of Allah"; the nominal clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the Name of Majesty is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).
﴿وَلِيُخْزِيَ﴾ the wāw conjoins to something implied; an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an أن concealed after the lām of reason (lām al-taʿlīl), the fāʿil being latent (mustatir). ﴿الْفاسِقِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from أن and the verb is in the position of the genitive by the lām, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted, implied verb.

daas-irab:6-6.t: ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is resumptive, and ما is a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿أَفاءَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb, and the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. ﴿عَلى رَسُولِهِ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فَما﴾ the fāʾ occurs in the response (jawāb) of the relative noun. ﴿ما﴾ negative. ﴿أَوْجَفْتُمْ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿مِنْ خَيْلٍ﴾ genitive in form by the redundant (zāʾida) من, accusative in position as mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿وَلا رِكابٍ﴾ conjoined to خيل. ﴿وَلكِنَّ اللَّهَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya); lākinna and its noun (ism). ﴿يُسَلِّطُ رُسُلَهُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its object, the fāʿil being latent (mustatir); the verbal clause is the khabar of لكن, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl. ﴿عَلى مَنْ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿يَشاءُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mubtadaʾ. ﴿عَلى كُلِّ﴾ both attached to قدير. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿قَدِيرٌ﴾ khabar; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:7-7.t:
﴿ما﴾ a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿أَفاءَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. ﴿عَلى رَسُولِهِ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿مِنْ أَهْلِ﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿الْقُرى﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿فَلِلَّهِ﴾ the fāʾ occurs in the response (jawāb) of the relative noun, and لله: both attached to an omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is the khabar of ما, and the clause ما أفاء.. is a badal (substitute) from the preceding one. ﴿وَلِلرَّسُولِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it, and ﴿لِذِي الْقُرْبى، وَالْيَتامى، وَالْمَساكِينِ، وَابْنِ السَّبِيلِ﴾: the words are conjoined to what precedes them. ﴿كَيْ لا يَكُونَ﴾ لا is negative, and a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by كي, its noun (ism) latent (mustatir). ﴿دُولَةً﴾ the khabar of يكون. ﴿بَيْنَ﴾ an adverb (ẓarf) of place. ﴿الْأَغْنِياءِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ both attached to an omitted ḥāl. ﴿وَما﴾ a jussive conditional noun, a fronted second mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿آتاكُمُ﴾ a past verb and its first object. ﴿الرَّسُولُ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿فَخُذُوهُ﴾ an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿وَما نَهاكُمْ عَنْهُ فَانْتَهُوا﴾ conjoined, and the i'rab is the same.
﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ an imperative verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ﴾ inna, its noun and its khabar. ﴿الْعِقابِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause gives the reason (taʿlīl).

daas-irab:8-8.t: ﴿لِلْفُقَراءِ﴾ a badal (substitute) from His words: لذي القربى. ﴿الْمُهاجِرِينَ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of الفقراء. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a second ṣifa. ﴿أُخْرِجُوا﴾ a passive past verb and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿مِنْ دِيارِهِمْ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿وَأَمْوالِهِمْ﴾ conjoined to ديارهم. ﴿يَبْتَغُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فَضْلًا﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿وَرِضْواناً﴾ conjoined to فضلا. ﴿وَيَنْصُرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, its object. [Translator's note: the source prints the word as ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ with kasra; as object the Quranic text has ﴿اللَّهَ﴾.] ﴿وَرَسُولَهُ﴾ conjoined to الله; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿هُمُ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿الصَّادِقُونَ﴾ khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:9-9.t:
﴿وَالَّذِينَ﴾ a conjunction and a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿تَبَوَّؤُا الدَّارَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَالْإِيمانَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of an omitted verb, and the implied clause is conjoined to تبوؤوا. ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿يُحِبُّونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of الذين, and the clause الذين.. is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿مِنْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿هاجَرَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila. ﴿إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿وَلا يَجِدُونَ﴾ لا is negative, and an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فِي صُدُورِهِمْ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿حاجَةً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مِمَّا﴾ both attached to an omitted ṣifa (adjective) of حاجة. ﴿أُوتُوا﴾ a passive past verb and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَيُؤْثِرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ﴾ both attached to the verb; the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). ﴿لَوْ﴾ connective (waṣliyya). ﴿كانَ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿بِهِمْ﴾ a fronted khabar. ﴿خَصاصَةٌ﴾ the postponed noun (ism) of كان; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ conditional, mubtadaʾ. ﴿يُوقَ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the dropping of the weak letter because it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ), and the nāʾib fāʿil is latent. ﴿شُحَّ نَفْسِهِ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi, annexed to نفسه; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿فَأُولئِكَ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa). ﴿أولئك﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿هُمُ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿الْمُفْلِحُونَ﴾ khabar; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), and the clauses of the condition and the apodosis are the khabar of من.

daas-irab:10-10.t: ﴿وَالَّذِينَ جاؤُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject), and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of الذين. ﴿مِنْ بَعْدِهِمْ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of الذين, and the clause الذين.. is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿رَبَّنَا﴾ the one addressed in the vocative (munādā), muḍāf. ﴿اغْفِرْ﴾ a verb of supplication (fiʿl duʿāʾ), its fāʿil latent (mustatir); the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying). ﴿لَنا﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿وَلِإِخْوانِنَا﴾ conjoined to لنا. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of إخواننا. ﴿سَبَقُونا﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿بِالْإِيمانِ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿وَلا تَجْعَلْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive لا. ﴿فِي قُلُوبِنا﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿غِلًّا﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ both attached to غلا. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila, and the clause لا تجعل.. is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿رَبَّنَا﴾ the one addressed in the vocative, muḍāf. ﴿إِنَّكَ رَؤُفٌ رَحِيمٌ﴾ inna, its noun (ism) and its two khabars; the nominal clause gives the reason (taʿlīl) for the supplication.

daas-irab:11-11.t: ﴿أَلَمْ﴾ the hamza is an interrogative particle. ﴿تَرَ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by لم, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿إِلَى الَّذِينَ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿نافَقُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿لِإِخْوانِهِمُ﴾ both attached to يقولون. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of إخوانهم. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of الذين. ﴿مِنْ أَهْلِ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿الْكِتابِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿لَئِنْ﴾ the lām paves the way for the oath (mūṭṭiʾa lil-qasam), and إن is conditional. ﴿أُخْرِجْتُمْ﴾ a passive past verb and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿لَنَخْرُجَنَّ﴾ the lām occurs in the response to the oath, and an imperfect verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis, and the nūn of emphasis is a particle with no grammatical position; the clause is the response to the oath (jawāb al-qasam), with no grammatical position. ﴿مَعَكُمْ﴾ an adverb (ẓarf) of place. ﴿وَلا نُطِيعُ﴾ لا is negative, and an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿فِيكُمْ﴾ both attached to the verb. ﴿أَحَداً﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿أَبَداً﴾ an adverb of time. ﴿وَإِنْ﴾ conditional. ﴿قُوتِلْتُمْ﴾ a passive past verb and the nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿لَنَنْصُرَنَّكُمْ﴾ the lām occurs in the response to the oath, and an imperfect verb, indeclinable on fatḥa because it is attached to the heavy nūn of emphasis; the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted because the oath indicates it, and the clause is the response to the oath, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَاللَّهُ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle, and the Name of Majesty is a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿يَشْهَدُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿إِنَّهُمْ لَكاذِبُونَ﴾ inna and its noun (ism), the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa), and كاذبون is its khabar; the clause is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi.

daas-irab:12-12.t: ﴿لَئِنْ﴾ its i'rab has preceded. ﴿أُخْرِجُوا﴾ a passive past verb and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿لا يَخْرُجُونَ﴾ لا is negative, and an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the response to the oath (jawāb al-qasam), with no grammatical position, and the clause أخرجوا is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿مَعَهُمْ﴾ an adverb (ẓarf) of place. ﴿وَلَئِنْ قُوتِلُوا لا يَنْصُرُونَهُمْ﴾ its i'rab has preceded. ﴿وَلَئِنْ نَصَرُوهُمْ﴾ its i'rab has also preceded. ﴿لَيُوَلُّنَّ﴾ the lām occurs in the response to the oath, and a passive imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, which is omitted because of the succession of like letters, and the omitted wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil. ﴿الْأَدْبارَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the response to the oath, with no grammatical position. [Translator's note: the source calls the verb passive (mabnī lil-majhūl); in the Quranic ﴿لَيُوَلُّنَّ الْأَدْبارَ﴾ the verb is active and the wāw is its fāʿil.] ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿لا يُنْصَرُونَ﴾ لا is negative, and a passive imperfect verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:13-13.t: ﴿لَأَنْتُمْ أَشَدُّ﴾ the lām is the lām of inception (lām al-ibtidāʾ), and a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate). ﴿رَهْبَةً﴾ tamyīz (specification); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿فِي صُدُورِهِمْ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) رهبة. ﴿مِنَ اللَّهِ﴾ both also attached to رهبة. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿بِأَنَّهُمْ﴾ the bāʾ is a preposition, and anna and its noun (ism). ﴿قَوْمٌ﴾ its khabar; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from أن and what follows it is in the position of the genitive by the bāʾ, and the preposition and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted khabar of the mubtadaʾ; the clause ذلك.. is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿لا يَفْقَهُونَ﴾ لا is negative, and an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is a ṣifa (adjective) of قوم.

daas-irab:14-14.t: ﴿لا يُقاتِلُونَكُمْ﴾ لا is negative, and an imperfect verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿جَمِيعاً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿فِي قُرىً﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿مُحَصَّنَةٍ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of قرى. ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction. ﴿مِنْ وَراءِ﴾ both conjoined to what precedes them. ﴿جُدُرٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿بَأْسُهُمْ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ an adverb (ẓarf) of place. ﴿شَدِيدٌ﴾ khabar (predicate). ﴿تَحْسَبُهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its first object, the fāʿil being latent (mustatir). ﴿جَمِيعاً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya). ﴿قُلُوبُهُمْ شَتَّى﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿بِأَنَّهُمْ قَوْمٌ لا يَعْقِلُونَ﴾ the i'rab of its counterpart has preceded.

daas-irab:15-15.t: ﴿كَمَثَلِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, both attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ both attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿قَرِيباً﴾ an adverb (ẓarf) of time. ﴿ذاقُوا وَبالَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object. ﴿أَمْرِهِمْ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿وَلَهُمْ﴾ a fronted khabar. ﴿عَذابٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿أَلِيمٌ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of عذاب; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:16-16.t: ﴿كَمَثَلِ﴾ its i'rab has preceded. ﴿الشَّيْطانِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb (ẓarf) for past time. ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation (iḍāfa). ﴿لِلْإِنْسانِ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿اكْفُرْ﴾ an imperative verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl (object of the saying). ﴿فَلَمَّا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and لما is an adverb of time (ẓarfiyya ḥīniyya). ﴿كَفَرَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿قالَ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil latent; the clause قال is the response (jawāb) of لما, with no grammatical position. ﴿إِنِّي﴾ inna and its noun (ism). ﴿بَرِيءٌ﴾ its khabar (predicate). ﴿مِنْكَ﴾ both attached to بريء; the clause is the maqūl al-qawl. ﴿إِنِّي﴾ inna and its noun. ﴿أَخافُ﴾ an imperfect verb, its fāʿil latent; the verbal clause is the khabar of إن. ﴿اللَّهَ﴾ the Name of Majesty, mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿رَبَّ﴾ a badal (substitute) from الله. ﴿الْعالَمِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi.

daas-irab:17-17.t: ﴿فَكانَ﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle, and a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb. ﴿عاقِبَتَهُما﴾ the fronted khabar (predicate) of كان. ﴿أَنَّهُما﴾ anna and its noun (ism). ﴿فِي النَّارِ﴾ its khabar; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) from أن, its noun and its khabar is in the position of the nominative as the postponed noun of كان. ﴿خالِدَيْنِ﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فِيها﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) خالدين. ﴿وَذلِكَ جَزاءُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar. ﴿الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:18-18.t: ﴿يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾ its i'rab has preceded. ﴿اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ an imperative verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَلْتَنْظُرْ﴾ an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command (lām al-amr); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿نَفْسٌ﴾ fāʿil. ﴿ما﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿قَدَّمَتْ﴾ a past verb, its fāʿil latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. ﴿لِغَدٍ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿إِنَّ اللَّهَ خَبِيرٌ﴾ inna, its noun (ism) and its khabar (predicate); the clause gives the reason (taʿlīl). ﴿بِما﴾ both attached to خبير. ﴿تَعْمَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila.

daas-irab:19-19.t: ﴿وَلا تَكُونُوا﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive لا, and the wāw is its noun (ism). ﴿كَالَّذِينَ﴾ its khabar (predicate). ﴿نَسُوا اللَّهَ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the Name of Majesty is its object; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿فَأَنْساهُمْ﴾ a past verb and its first object, the fāʿil being latent (mustatir). ﴿أَنْفُسَهُمْ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿هُمُ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿الْفاسِقُونَ﴾ khabar; the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:20-20.t:
﴿لا﴾ negative. ﴿يَسْتَوِي أَصْحابُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿النَّارِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.
﴿وَأَصْحابُ الْجَنَّةِ﴾ conjoined to أصحاب النار. ﴿أَصْحابُ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿الْجَنَّةِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿هُمُ﴾ a pronoun of separation (ḍamīr faṣl). ﴿الْفائِزُونَ﴾ khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:21-21.t: ﴿لَوْ﴾ a non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿أَنْزَلْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent). ﴿هذَا﴾ the demonstrative is its object. ﴿الْقُرْآنَ﴾ a badal (substitute) from the demonstrative; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿عَلى جَبَلٍ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿لَرَأَيْتَهُ﴾ the lām is connective (rābiṭa), and a past verb, its fāʿil and its object; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position. ﴿خاشِعاً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative (manṣūb). ﴿مُتَصَدِّعاً﴾ a second ḥāl. ﴿مِنْ خَشْيَةِ﴾ both attached to خاشعا. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَتِلْكَ﴾ the demonstrative is a mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿الْأَمْثالُ﴾ a badal. ﴿نَضْرِبُها﴾ an imperfect verb and its object, the fāʿil being latent (mustatir). ﴿لِلنَّاسِ﴾ both attached to the verb; the verbal clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ﴾ laʿalla and its noun (ism). ﴿يَتَفَكَّرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the verbal clause is the khabar of لعل, and the nominal clause gives the reason (taʿlīl).

daas-irab:22-22.t: ﴿هُوَ اللَّهُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿الَّذِي﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of the Name of Majesty. ﴿لا﴾ the lā of generic negation. ﴿إِلهَ﴾ its noun (ism), indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of the accusative, and its khabar is omitted. ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿هُوَ﴾ a badal (substitute) from the latent (mustatir) pronoun in the omitted khabar; the nominal clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿عالِمُ﴾ a second khabar. ﴿الْغَيْبِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَالشَّهادَةِ﴾ conjoined to الغيب. ﴿هُوَ﴾ mubtadaʾ. ﴿الرَّحْمنُ الرَّحِيمُ﴾ two khabars; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:23-23.t: ﴿هُوَ اللَّهُ الَّذِي لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ﴾: its i'rab has preceded. ﴿الْمَلِكُ الْقُدُّوسُ، السَّلامُ الْمُؤْمِنُ الْمُهَيْمِنُ الْعَزِيزُ الْجَبَّارُ الْمُتَكَبِّرُ﴾ khabars (predicates) of the Name of Majesty. ﴿سُبْحانَ﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object) of an omitted verb. ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ the Name of Majesty, muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). [Translator's note: the source prints the word as ﴿اللَّهُ﴾ with ḍamma; as muḍāf ilayhi the Quranic text has ﴿اللَّهِ﴾.] ﴿عَمَّا﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) سبحان. ﴿يُشْرِكُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause).

daas-irab:24-24.t: ﴿هُوَ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿اللَّهُ الْخالِقُ الْبارِئُ الْمُصَوِّرُ﴾ khabars (predicates) of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿لَهُ﴾ a fronted khabar. ﴿الْأَسْماءُ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ. ﴿الْحُسْنى﴾ a ṣifa (adjective); the nominal clause is a fourth khabar of the mubtadaʾ. ﴿يُسَبِّحُ﴾ an imperfect verb. ﴿لَهُ﴾ both attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿ما﴾ fāʿil (agent); the verbal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿فِي السَّماواتِ﴾ both attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun. ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾ conjoined to السموات. ﴿وَهُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْحَكِيمُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and two khabars; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).

farraa:2-2.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿هُوَ ٱلَّذِيۤ أَخْرَجَ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَابِ مِن دِيَارِهِمْ﴾.
These are the Banū al-Naḍīr. They had made a pact with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that they would be neither with him nor against him. When the Muslims suffered their setback on the day of Uḥud, they acted treacherously: Ḥuyayy ibn Akhṭab rode to Abū Sufyān and his companions among the people of Mecca, and they made a pact against the Prophet ﷺ. Revelation came to him about that, and he said to the Muslims: "I have been commanded to kill Ḥuyayy." A party of the Muslims volunteered for it and killed him. The Prophet ﷺ went out against them in the morning, and they fortified themselves in their houses; they began boring through (the walls of) one house into another that was better fortified, and pelting the Prophet ﷺ with the stones they took out of it; and the Muslims began demolishing their houses to widen the place of fighting. That is His saying [Mighty and Majestic]: ﴿يُخْرِبُونَ بُيُوتَهُمْ بِأَيْدِيهِمْ وَأَيْدِي ٱلْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾. The readers agreed on (يُخْرِبون), except ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī, who read (يخرّبون). «يخرّبون» is as it were «يهدّمون» (they demolish), and «يُخْرِبون», without shadda, means: they go out of them and leave them (deserted). Do you not see that they were boring through the houses and so leaving them unusable? That is the meaning of (يُخْرِبون). Those who said (يخرّبون) took it in the sense of the demolition the Muslims were carrying out. All of it is correct, and the agreed reading of the readers is dearer to me.
«[Translator's note: the reader is elsewhere called «أبو عبد الرحمن السلمى»; the source here has «عبدالرحمن السلمى».]»
[And His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿فَٱعْتَبِرُواْ يٰأُوْلِي ٱلأَبْصَارِ﴾: O possessors of minds. And it is said: «يا أولى الأبصار» means: O you who witnessed that with your own eyes.]
And His saying: ﴿لأَوَّلِ ٱلْحَشْرِ ﴾.
[They were] the first to be expelled from the Arabian peninsula, which is the Hijaz.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying: ﴿مَا قَطَعْتُمْ مِّن لِّينَةٍ﴾.
Al-Farrāʾ told us: Ḥibbān told me, from al-Kalbī, from Abū Ṣāliḥ, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: the Prophet ﷺ ordered all the palm trees to be cut down that day — meaning the day of the Banū al-Naḍīr — except the ʿajwa. Ibn ʿAbbās said: every kind of palm other than the ʿajwa is «اللين».
Al-Farrāʾ said: its singular is «لِينة». In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "ما قطعتم من لِينَةٍ ولا تركتم قُوَّماً على أصوله إلا بإذن الله"; He is saying: except by the command of Allah.
And His saying: ﴿أُصوله﴾.
He took «اللين» as a whole collectively (with a masculine pronoun); and whoever said «أُصُولها» took «النخل» as feminine, because it is treated as masculine and feminine.

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿فَمَآ أَوْجَفْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ خَيْلٍ وَلاَ رِكَابٍ﴾.
The Prophet ﷺ had secured the spoils of Banū al-Naḍīr, Qurayẓa and Fadak. The chiefs said to him: "Take your choice portion of this and allot us the fourth." Then the explanation came: these are villages which they did not fight for with horses, and to which they did not travel on camels; you only walked to them on your feet — there were two miles between them and Medina. So the Prophet ﷺ gave them to some of the Emigrants who were in need and had been present at Badr.

farraa:7-7.t:
Then He said: ﴿مَّآ أَفَآءَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ رَسُولِهِ مِنْ أَهْلِ ٱلْقُرَىٰ﴾.
These three; it belongs purely to Allah and the Messenger.
Then He said: ﴿وَلِذِي ٱلْقُرْبَىٰ﴾:
for the kin of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; ﴿وَٱلْيَتَامَىٰ﴾: the orphans of the Muslims in general, among them the orphans of the Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib; ﴿وَٱلْمَسَاكِينِ﴾: the poor of the Muslims, not including the poor of the Banū ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib.
Then He said: «كَىْ لا يَكُونَ ذلك الفَىء دُولة بين الأغنياء» — the chiefs — to be dealt with as it was dealt with in the Jāhiliyya. And concerning the chiefs there came down: ﴿وَمَآ آتَاكُمُ ٱلرَّسُولُ فَخُذُوهُ وَمَا نَهَاكُمْ عَنْهُ فَٱنتَهُواْ﴾, and they were content. As for «الدُّولة», the people read it with a ḍamma on the dāl, except al-Sulamī — as far as I know — who read «دَولة» with a fatḥa. This is not the place for «الدَّولة»: «الدَّولة» applies to two armies, where this one routs that one and then the victor is routed, so you say: «the turn (al-dawla) has come back against these», as though it were a single occasion. «الدُّولة» applies to possession (of wealth) and to customs that change and alternate over time; that is «الدُّولة».
Some of the Arabs read (دولةٌ) (nominative), but most of them read it accusative; and some (read) «يكون», and some «تكون».

farraa:9-9.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ تَبَوَّءُوا ٱلدَّارَ وَٱلإِيمَانَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ﴾.
He means the Anṣār, who love those who emigrated to them. When the Emigrants were given what the Prophet ﷺ apportioned to them of the spoils (fayʾ) of the Banū al-Naḍīr, he did not feel sure that others would not envy them, since he had not apportioned anything to them. So the Prophet ﷺ said to the Anṣār: "If you wish, you will share with them from your houses and your property, and I will apportion to you as I have apportioned to them; or else the share will be theirs, and you keep your houses and your property." They said: "No; rather you apportion to them from our houses and our property, and we will not share with them in the allotment." So Allah, Majestic and Mighty, revealed these verses in praise of the Anṣār, saying: ﴿يُحِبُّونَ مَنْ هَاجَرَ إِلَيْهِمْ﴾ — meaning the Emigrants — ﴿وَلاَ يَجِدُونَ فِي صُدُورِهِمْ﴾ to the end of the verse.

farraa:10-10.t: In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh, ﴿وَٱلَّذِينَ جَآءُوا مِن بَعْدِهِمْ﴾ — meaning the Emigrants — (continues): «يقولون ربَّنا اغفِرْ لنا ولإخواننا الذين تبوءوا الإيمان من قبل، وألّف بين قلوبنا، ولا تجعل فيها غَمَرا للذين آمنوا» (they say: our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who settled in faith before, unite our hearts, and put in them no rancour towards those who believe).

farraa:13-14.t:
His saying: ﴿لأَنتُمْ أَشَدُّ رَهْبَةً فِي صُدُورِهِمْ﴾.
He is saying: you, O company of Muslims, are more feared in their breasts [meaning the Banū al-Naḍīr] than the punishment of Allah is in their view. That is because the Banū al-Naḍīr were people of might, but Allah cast terror of the Muslims into their hearts. Concerning that came down: ﴿تَحْسَبُهُمْ﴾ — meaning the Banū al-Naḍīr — united, while their hearts differ. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: «وقلوبهم أشت», that is: more divided.
«[Translator's note: «جيمعاً» in the source is a misprint for «جميعاً».]»
And His saying: ﴿أَوْ مِن وَرَآءِ جُدُرٍ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās read «جدار» (a wall), and the rest of the readers «جدر» in the plural.

farraa:17-17.t:
His saying: ﴿فَكَانَ عَاقِبَتَهُمَآ أَنَّهُمَا فِي ٱلنَّارِ خَالِدِينَ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: «فكان عاقبتهُما أنهما خالدان فى النار» (nominative). In [196/ب] our reading ﴿خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا﴾ is accusative. I do not like the nominative, even though it is permissible. That is because the adverbial phrase (ṣifa) has referred back to the Fire twice, and the meaning is about the abiding. So when you see the (participial) predicate between two adverbial phrases, one of which refers back to the place of the other, you put the predicate in the accusative; and this is of that kind. Similar in speech is your saying: «مررت برجل على بابه متحملا به» (I passed a man at whose door (someone was) loading up at it). Similar is the poet's saying:
والزعفرانُ على ترائبُها * شَرِقاً به اللباتُ والنحْرُ
(And saffron is on her breast-bones, her upper chest and throat drenched with it.)
For «الترائب» here are «اللبات», so the adverbial phrase came back with its noun on which it fell first. But when the two adverbial phrases differ, both the nominative and the accusative are permissible and good. Of that is your saying: «عبدالله فى الدار راغبٌ فيك» (ʿAbd Allāh is in the house, desiring you).
Do you not see that the «فى» in «فى الدار» differs from the «فى» that goes with the desire? The proof by which the accusative is distinguished from the nominative is: do you see (whether) the latter phrase can come before the first? Thus you say: «هذا أخوك فى يده درهم قابضا عليه» (this is your brother, in his hand is a dirham, grasping it); but if you said «هذا أخوك قابضاً عليه فى يده درهم», it would not be permissible. And you say: «هذا رجل فى يده درهم قائمٌ إلى زيد» (this is a man with a dirham in his hand, standing towards Zayd); do you not see that you can say «هذا رجل قائم إلى زيد فى يده درهم»? So this indicates the accusative when putting the latter (phrase) first is impossible, and indicates the nominative when putting the latter first is easy.
«[Translator's note: in the verse the source prints «ترائبُها» with a ḍamma; the genitive «ترائبِها» is expected after «على».]»

farraa:20-20.t:
His saying: ﴿لاَ يَسْتَوِيۤ أَصْحَابُ ٱلنَّارِ وَأَصْحَابُ ٱلْجَنَّةِ﴾.
In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: «ولا أصحاب النار»; «لا» is a ṣila (redundant connective) when there is a negation at the beginning of the statement and it is connected by «لا» at its end. One of the Banū Kilāb recited:
إرادة ألاّ يجمع الله بيننا * ولا بينها أخرى الليالى الغوابر
(Wishing that Allah should not bring us together, nor her, until the last of the remaining nights.)
Its meaning is: wishing that Allah should not bring us and her together; so he connected with «لا».
«[Translator's note: «وأنشد فى بعض بنى كلاب» is as printed, evidently for «وأنشد بعض بنى كلاب».]»

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Ḥashr
Medinan
﷽
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ ما في السَّماواتِ وما في الأرْضِ وهو العَزِيزُ الحَكِيمُ﴾ — Allah opened the sūra by mentioning His sanctification, and that He has things which declare Him free of evil. Similar to that is His saying: ﴿وَإنْ مِن شَيْءٍ إلا يُسَبِّحُ بِحَمْدِهِ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 44].

zajjaj:2-2.t: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي أخْرَجَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِن أهْلِ الكِتابِ﴾ (the verse) — these are the Banū al-Naḍīr, who had might and strength among the Jews; so people thought that, because of their might and strength, they would not be driven out of their homes, and the Banū al-Naḍīr thought that their fortresses would protect them from Allah, that is, from the command of Allah. ﴿فَأتاهُمُ اللَّهُ مِن حَيْثُ لَمْ يَحْتَسِبُوا وقَذَفَ في قُلُوبِهِمُ الرُّعْبَ﴾: when the Prophet, upon him be peace, entered Medina, the Banū al-Naḍīr made a pact with him that they would be neither against him nor with him. Then when the day of "Uḥud" came and the idolaters gained the upper hand over the Muslims, they broke the pact and doubt entered them. Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf was their chief; he went out with sixty men to Mecca and made a pact with the idolaters to back one another against the Prophet, upon him be peace. Allah informed His Prophet, upon him be peace, of that. When he (Kaʿb) arrived back in Medina, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Muḥammad ibn Maslama to kill him. Muḥammad ibn Maslama was Kaʿb's foster-brother. Muḥammad ibn Maslama asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for permission to speak ill of him so that Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf would be beguiled (li-yaʿtarra) [Translator's note: so in the text; presumably li-yaghtarra, "be lulled into trust"]. So Muḥammad came to him with a group, called him down from his dwelling and made him imagine that he had been pressed hard over the taking of the ṣadaqa (alms) from him. When he came down, Muḥammad ibn Maslama seized him by his forelock and cried "Allāhu akbar", and his companions came out and killed him on the spot. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out in the morning to campaign against the Banū al-Naḍīr and laid siege to them; it has been said that he campaigned against them on a donkey haltered with palm-fibre. The believers were demolishing parts of the dwellings of the Banū al-Naḍīr so that they would have places to fight from, and the Banū al-Naḍīr were demolishing their dwellings in order to block the entrances of their lanes with them, so that nothing would be left for the believers. Then Allah cast terror into their hearts: ﴿يُخْرِبُونَ بُيُوتَهم بِأيْدِيهِمْ وأيْدِي المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾; the meaning of their destruction by the hands of the believers is that they exposed them to that. So they parted from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ on the terms of evacuating their dwellings and carrying whatever their camels could bear, except silver and gold. So they emigrated to Syria (al-Shām); a group of them went to Khaybar and a group to al-Ḥīra. That is His saying: ﴿هُوَ الَّذِي أخْرَجَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِن أهْلِ الكِتابِ مِن دِيارِهِمْ لأوَّلِ الحَشْرِ﴾. It was the first gathering (ḥashr) to be gathered to Syria; then creation will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection to Syria; that is why it was said "لِأوَّلِ الحَشْرِ" (at the first gathering). So all the Jews and Christians are to be expelled from the Arabian Peninsula. It is transmitted from ʿUmar that the Prophet ﷺ said: «"I shall surely expel the Jews from the Arabian Peninsula."» Al-Khalīl said: "The Arabian Peninsula is their native ground and their dwelling-place." It was called "جَزِيرَةُ العَرَبِ" (the island of the Arabs) only because the sea of al-Ḥabs [Translator's note: so in the text; presumably al-Ḥabash, i.e. the Red Sea], the sea of Persia, the Tigris and the Euphrates surround it; so it is their land and their native ground. Abū ʿUbayda said: the Arabian Peninsula extends from Ḥafr Abī Mūsā to Yemen in length, and from the sands of Yabrīn to the edge of al-Samāwa in breadth [Translator's note: the text has "جَفْرِ أبِي مُوسى" and "بَيْرِينَ"]. Al-Aṣmaʿī said: to the farthest point of ʿAdan Abyan, to the extremities of Yemen, until it reaches the edges of the deserts of Syria.

zajjaj:5-5.t:
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿ما قَطَعْتُمْ مِن لِينَةٍ أوْ تَرَكْتُمُوها قائِمَةً عَلى أُصُولِها﴾ — that is: whatever palm tree you cut down. All palm trees, except the barnī and the ʿajwa, are called by the people of Medina "اَلْألْوانَ" (the varieties). The origin of "لِينَةٌ" is "لِوْنَةٌ": the wāw was changed to yāʾ because of the kasra before it, and so it was said "لِينَةٌ".
The Banū al-Naḍīr objected to the cutting down of the palms, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that this — the cutting and the leaving, both — was by His permission. ﴿وَلِيُخْزِيَ الفاسِقِينَ﴾: by showing them their wealth being disposed of by the Muslims however they liked.

zajjaj:6-6.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَما أفاءَ اللَّهُ عَلى رَسُولِهِ مِنهم فَما أوْجَفْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِن خَيْلٍ ولا رِكابٍ﴾ — He means: "what Allah gave as fayʾ (spoils gained without fighting) to His Messenger from the Banū al-Naḍīr, against which they did not urge on horses or riding camels". Al-rikāb are camels, and "اَلْوَجِيفُ" is a pace of travel below the taqrīb (a quick trot); one says "وَجَفَ الفَرَسُ" (the horse went at a wajīf) and "أوْجَفْتُهُ" (I urged it on). The meaning is that you have no share in it; it belongs purely to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who does with it as he likes. Likewise everything conquered by the imams against which the Muslims did not urge on horses or riding camels.

zajjaj:7-7.t: His saying: ﴿ما أفاءَ اللَّهُ عَلى رَسُولِهِ مِن أهْلِ القُرى فَلِلَّهِ ولِلرَّسُولِ﴾ — the meaning of ﴿فَلِلَّهِ﴾ is: it is His to command you concerning it as He wills. ﴿وَلِلرَّسُولِ ولِذِي القُرْبى﴾: He means the relatives of the Prophet ﷺ, because they have been barred from charity (ṣadaqa), so a right in the fayʾ was assigned to them; ﴿واليَتامى والمَساكِينِ وابْنِ السَّبِيلِ كَيْ لا يَكُونَ دُولَةً بَيْنَ الأغْنِياءِ مِنكُمْ﴾.

zajjaj:8-8.t: His saying: ﴿لِلْفُقَراءِ المُهاجِرِينَ﴾ — He made clear who the poor are who have the right, and said: ﴿الَّذِينَ أُخْرِجُوا مِن دِيارِهِمْ وأمْوالِهِمْ﴾.

zajjaj:9-9.t:
His saying: ﴿والَّذِينَ تَبَوَّءُوا الدّارَ﴾ — He means the Anṣār.
﴿والإيمانَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ﴾ — He means the Muhājirūn. ﴿يُحِبُّونَ مَن هاجَرَ إلَيْهِمْ﴾, that is: the Anṣār love the believers. ﴿وَلا يَجِدُونَ في صُدُورِهِمْ حاجَةً مِمّا أُوتُوا﴾, that is: the Anṣār find in their breasts no need (envy) for what the Muhājirūn are given.
His saying: ﴿وَيُؤْثِرُونَ عَلى أنْفُسِهِمْ ولَوْ كانَ بِهِمْ خَصاصَةٌ﴾ — Abū Isḥāq [Translator's note: i.e. al-Zajjāj himself] said: as for what Allah gave as fayʾ to His Messenger from the people of the towns, such as Khaybar and the like, the practice among the people of the Ḥijāz in dividing the fayʾ is that it is distributed among these named categories in proportion to what the imam sees fit, aiming at what is best in that, if the imam sees fit to do that; and if he sees that one of the categories needs the whole fayʾ, he spends it on that category, or on these categories in proportion to what he sees fit.
His saying: ﴿كَيْ لا يَكُونَ دُولَةً بَيْنَ الأغْنِياءِ مِنكُمْ﴾ [al-Ḥashr: 7] — it is read with ḍamma on the dāl and with fatḥa. "اَلدُّولَةُ" is the name of the thing that is passed around, and "اَلدَّوْلَةُ" is the act, and the shifting from one state to another. It has also been read "دُولَةٌ" in the nominative (rafʿ). Whoever reads "كَيْلا يَكُونَ دُولَةٌ" takes it according to the view of completeness [Translator's note: i.e. yakūnu as the complete (tāmma) verb, "come to be"]; and it is also possible that "دُولَةٌ" be the ism (subject) of "يَكُونَ" and its khabar (predicate) be "بَيْنَ الأغْنِياءِ". The more common is ﴿كَيْ لا يَكُونَ دُولَةً بَيْنَ الأغْنِياءِ مِنكُمْ﴾ [al-Ḥashr: 7], on the meaning: "so that the fayʾ should not be a dūla", that is, something passed around.
His saying: ﴿وَما آتاكُمُ الرَّسُولُ فَخُذُوهُ﴾ [al-Ḥashr: 7], that is: of the fayʾ; ﴿وَما نَهاكم عَنْهُ﴾ [al-Ḥashr: 7], that is: from taking it; ﴿فانْتَهُوا﴾ [al-Ḥashr: 7].

zajjaj:10-10.t: His saying: ﴿والَّذِينَ جاءُوا مِن بَعْدِهِمْ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنا اغْفِرْ لَنا﴾ — that is: what Allah gave as fayʾ to His Messenger from the people of the towns belongs to Allah, to His Messenger, to these Muslims, and to those who come after them until the Day of Resurrection, as long as they remain in love of the Companions of the Messenger of Allah, upon him be peace. The evidence for that is His saying: ﴿والَّذِينَ جاءُوا مِن بَعْدِهِمْ﴾ in the state of their saying: ﴿رَبَّنا اغْفِرْ لَنا ولإخْوانِنا الَّذِينَ سَبَقُونا بِالإيمانِ﴾ (the verse). So whoever invokes mercy upon the Companions of the Messenger of Allah, and has no rancour in his heart towards any of them, has a share in the fayʾ of the Muslims; and whoever reviles them and does not invoke mercy upon them, or has rancour in his heart towards them, Allah has not assigned him a right in anything of the fayʾ of the Muslims. This is the explicit text of the Book, clear.

zajjaj:11-11.t:
His saying: ﴿ألَمْ تَرَ إلى الَّذِينَ نافَقُوا يَقُولُونَ لإخْوانِهِمُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِن أهْلِ الكِتابِ﴾ — they are their brothers, joined together by disbelief. ﴿لَئِنْ أُخْرِجْتُمْ لَنَخْرُجَنَّ مَعَكم ولا نُطِيعُ فِيكم أحَدًا أبَدًا وإنْ قُوتِلْتُمْ لَنَنْصُرَنَّكم واللَّهُ يَشْهَدُ إنَّهم لَكاذِبُونَ﴾: this became evident in the affair of the Banū al-Naḍīr, with whom the hypocrites had made a pact; for they were driven out of their homes and their wealth, yet the hypocrites did not go out with them, and they were fought, yet they did not help them; so Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, exposed their lying.
If someone says: what is the point of His saying ﴿وَلَئِنْ قُوتِلُوا لا يَنْصُرُونَهُمْ﴾ [al-Ḥashr: 12], and then His saying ﴿وَلَئِنْ نَصَرُوهم لَيُوَلُّنَّ الأدْبارَ ثُمَّ لا يُنْصَرُونَ﴾ [al-Ḥashr: 12]? The lexicographers have two views on this. They said: its meaning is: if they were to undertake to help them; or: "if those of them who remain were to help them, they would surely turn their backs."

zajjaj:14-14.t:
His saying: ﴿لا يُقاتِلُونَكم جَمِيعًا إلا في قُرًى مُحَصَّنَةٍ أوْ مِن وراءِ جُدُرٍ﴾ — it has been read "أوْ مِن وراءِ جِدارٍ", in the singular, and it has been read with sukūn on the dāl. Whoever reads "جُدُرٍ" takes it as the plural of "جِدارٌ": "جُدُرٌ", like "حِمارٌ" and "حُمُرٌ". Whoever reads with sukūn on the dāl has dropped the ḍamma because of its heaviness, as they said "صُحْفٌ" and "صُحُفٌ". Whoever reads "جِدارٍ" takes it as the singular. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that when they unite to fight you, because of the terror Allah has cast into their hearts, they do not come out openly to battle you; they fight only while fortified by towns and walls.
His saying: ﴿تَحْسَبُهم جَمِيعًا وقُلُوبُهم شَتّى﴾, that is: they are divided; their hearts are not alike, and they do not cooperate with united intentions, because Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is the helper of His party and the forsaker of His enemies.

zajjaj:15-15.t: His saying: ﴿كَمَثَلِ الَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِهِمْ قَرِيبًا ذاقُوا وبالَ أمْرِهِمْ ولَهم عَذابٌ ألِيمٌ﴾ — like what befell the people of "Badr".

zajjaj:16-16.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿كَمَثَلِ الشَّيْطانِ إذْ قالَ لِلإنْسانِ اكْفُرْ فَلَمّا كَفَرَ قالَ إنِّي بَرِيءٌ مِنكَ﴾ — that is: the likeness of the hypocrites in their deceiving the Banū al-Naḍīr, and their saying to them: ﴿لَئِنْ أُخْرِجْتُمْ لَنَخْرُجَنَّ مَعَكم ولا نُطِيعُ فِيكم أحَدًا أبَدًا وإنْ قُوتِلْتُمْ لَنَنْصُرَنَّكُمْ﴾ [al-Ḥashr: 11], is like the likeness of Satan when he said to man: "Disbelieve", and when he disbelieved he said: "I am quit of you". This is indicated, and Allah knows best, by His saying: ﴿وَإذْ زَيَّنَ لَهُمُ الشَّيْطانُ أعْمالَهم وقالَ لا غالِبَ لَكُمُ اليَوْمَ مِنَ النّاسِ وإنِّي جارٌ لَكم فَلَمّا تَراءَتِ الفِئَتانِ نَكَصَ عَلى عَقِبَيْهِ وقالَ إنِّي بَرِيءٌ مِنكُمْ﴾ [al-Anfāl: 48]. So likewise the hypocrites: when what befell the Banū al-Naḍīr befell them, they disowned them. It has come in the exegesis that there was a worshipper called "Barṣīṣā" who used to treat madness. He treated a woman and she pleased him, and Satan led him astray until he lay with her; then he killed her; then Satan disowned him. The story is long, but this is its gist.

zajjaj:17-17.t: His saying: ﴿فَكانَ عاقِبَتَهُما أنَّهُما في النّارِ خالِدَيْنِ فِيها﴾ — ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd read: "أنَّهُما في النّارِ خالِدانِ فِيها", which is permissible in Arabic, except that it differs from the Muṣḥaf. Whoever says ﴿خالِدَيْنِ فِيها﴾ makes it accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial); whoever reads "خالِدانِ" makes it the khabar (predicate) of "أنَّ". The reading is "فَكانَ عاقِبَتَهُما" [Translator's note: so in the text; by what follows, عاقِبَتَهُما here is accusative as the khabar of kāna], and the khabar of "كانَ" is "أنَّهُما في النّارِ", on the meaning: "their end was their being in the Fire". It is also read "فَكانَ عاقِبَتُهُما"; the accusative is better, with the ism (subject) of "كانَ" being "أنَّهُما". [Translator's note: the passage first says the reading is "on the ism of kāna" and that "أنَّهُما في النّارِ" is its khabar, then says that in the preferred accusative reading the ism is "أنَّهُما"; it is translated as it stands.]

zajjaj:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ ولْتَنْظُرْ نَفْسٌ ما قَدَّمَتْ لِغَدٍ﴾ — that is: for the Day of Resurrection; it was brought near to people, and so made as though it were coming tomorrow. The origin of "غَدٍ" is "غَدْوٍ", except that in the Quran it has come only with the wāw dropped. It has been spoken with the wāw dropped, and in poetry it has come both with the wāw retained and with it dropped. The poet said, retaining it:
وَما النّاسُ إلّا كالدِّيارِ وأهْلِها ∗∗∗ بِها يَوْمَ حُلْوِها وغَدْوًا بَلاقِعُ
(People are only like dwellings and their inhabitants: they are in them on the day they settle there, and tomorrow they are empty wastes)
Another said:
لا تَغْلُواها وادْلُواها دَلْوا ∗∗∗ إنَّ مَعَ اليَوْمِ أخاهُ غَدْوا
(Do not drive her too hard; lead her on gently, for with today comes its brother, tomorrow)

zajjaj:19-19.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلا تَكُونُوا كالَّذِينَ نَسُوا اللَّهَ فَأنْساهم أنْفُسَهُمْ﴾ — "نَسُوا اللَّهَ": they abandoned remembrance of Him and what He commanded them; so Allah abandoned remembering them with mercy and success (tawfīq).

zajjaj:21-21.t: His saying: ﴿لَوْ أنْـزَلْنا هَذا القُرْآنَ عَلى جَبَلٍ لَرَأيْتَهُ خاشِعًا مُتَصَدِّعًا مِن خَشْيَةِ اللَّهِ﴾ — Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that it belongs to the standing of the Quran, its greatness and its clarity, that if discernment were placed in a mountain as it has been placed in you, and the Quran were sent down upon it, it would humble itself and split apart out of fear of Allah. The meaning of "خَشَعَ" is: it lowered itself and submitted; and the meaning of "تَصَدَّعَ" is: it cracked apart. It is also possible that this be by way of parable, because of His saying: ﴿وَتِلْكَ الأمْثالُ نَضْرِبُها لِلنّاسِ﴾, as He said, Glory be to Him: ﴿لَقَدْ جِئْتُمْ شَيْئًا إدًّا﴾ [Maryam: 89] ﴿تَكادُ السَّماواتُ يَتَفَطَّرْنَ مِنهُ وتَنْشَقُّ الأرْضُ وتَخِرُّ الجِبالُ هَدًّا﴾ [Maryam: 90].

zajjaj:22-22.t: His saying: ﴿هُوَ اللَّهُ الَّذِي لا إلَهَ إلا هو عالِمُ الغَيْبِ والشَّهادَةِ﴾ — this refers back to the beginning of the sūra, to His saying: ﴿سَبَّحَ لِلَّهِ ما في السَّماواتِ وما في الأرْضِ وهو العَزِيزُ الحَكِيمُ﴾ [al-Ḥashr: 1], ﴿هُوَ اللَّهُ الَّذِي لا إلَهَ إلا هُوَ﴾.

zajjaj:23-23.t:
His saying: ﴿المَلِكُ القُدُّوسُ﴾ — "اَلْقُدُّوسُ" is the Pure; from this comes the expression "بَيْتُ المَقْدِسِ", that is: the house of the place in which one is purified of sins.
His saying: ﴿السَّلامُ﴾ is one of the names of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He; and it has been said: "اَلسَّلامُ" is the One from whose injustice creation is safe. ﴿المُؤْمِنُ﴾: the One who affirmed His own oneness by His saying: ﴿شَهِدَ اللَّهُ أنَّهُ لا إلَهَ إلا هو والمَلائِكَةُ وأُولُو العِلْمِ قائِمًا بِالقِسْطِ لا إلَهَ إلا هو العَزِيزُ الحَكِيمُ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 18]; and it has been said: "اَلْمُؤْمِنُ" is the One from whose injustice creation is secure.
His saying: ﴿العَزِيزُ﴾, that is: the Unassailable whom nothing overcomes. ﴿المُهَيْمِنُ﴾: it has come in the exegesis that it is the Witness, and it has come in the exegesis that it is the Trustworthy. Some lexicographers claimed that the hāʾ is a substitute (badal) for the hamza and that its origin is "اَلْمُؤَيْمِنُ", just as they said "إيّاكَ" and "هِيّاكَ". The exegesis bears witness to this view, because it has come that it is the Trustworthy and it has come that it is the Witness, and the interpretation of "the Witness" is: the one trustworthy in his testimony.
His saying: ﴿الجَبّارُ﴾ — its interpretation is: the One who compelled (jabara) creation to what He willed of His command.
His saying: ﴿المُتَكَبِّرُ﴾: the One who is too great to wrong His servants. ﴿سُبْحانَ اللَّهِ عَمّا يُشْرِكُونَ﴾ — its interpretation is: Allah is declared free of their associating partners (with Him).

zajjaj:24-24.t:
His saying: ﴿هُوَ اللَّهُ الخالِقُ البارِئُ المُصَوِّرُ﴾ — a reading has been transmitted which ought not to be read; it was transmitted as "اَلْبارِئَ المُصَوِّرَ", in the accusative, meaning: the One who created (baraʾa) Adam and gave him form.
His saying: ﴿لَهُ الأسْماءُ الحُسْنى﴾ — it has come in the exegesis that they are ninety-nine names, and whoever enumerates them enters Paradise; and it has come in the exegesis that the greatest name of Allah is "اَللَّهُ". We shall explain these names, and the derivation of those of them that ought to be explained, if Allah wills. Abū Hurayra al-Dawsī related from the Prophet, upon him be peace, that he said: «"Allah has a hundred names less one; whoever enumerates them enters Paradise. They are: اللَّهُ، الواحِدُ، الرَّحْمَنُ، الرَّحِيمُ، الأحَدُ، الصَّمَدُ، الفَرْدُ، السَّلامُ، المُؤْمِنُ، المُهَيْمِنُ، العَزِيزُ، الجَبّارُ، المُتَكَبِّرُ، الخالِقُ، البارِئُ، المُصَوِّرُ، الحَيُّ، القَيُّومُ، العَلِيُّ، الكَبِيرُ، الغَنِيُّ، الكَرِيمُ، الوَلِيُّ، الحَمِيدُ، العَلِيمُ، اللَّطِيفُ، السَّمِيعُ، البَصِيرُ، الوَدُودُ، الشَّكُورُ، الظّاهِرُ، الباطِنُ، الأوَّلُ، الآخِرُ، المُبْدِئُ، البَدِيعُ، المَلِكُ، القُدُّوسُ، الذّارِئُ، الفاصِلُ، الغَفُورُ، المَجِيدُ، الحَلِيمُ، الحَفِيظُ، الشَّهِيدُ، الرَّبُّ، القَدِيرُ، التَّوّابُ، الحافِظُ، الكَفِيلُ، القَرِيبُ، المُجِيبُ، العَظِيمُ، الجَلِيلُ، العَفُوُّ، الصَّفُوحُ، الحَقُّ، المُبِينُ، المُعِزُّ، المُذِلُّ، القَوِيُّ، الشَّدِيدُ، الحَنّانُ، المَنّانُ، الفَتّاحُ، الرَّؤُوفُ، القابِضُ، الباسِطُ، الباعِثُ، الوارِثُ، الدَّيّانُ، الفاضِلُ، الرَّقِيبُ، الحَسِيبُ، المَتِينُ، الوَكِيلُ، الزَّكِيُّ، الطّاهِرُ، المُحْسِنُ، المُجْمَلُ، المُبارَكُ، السُّبُّوحُ، الحَكِيمُ، البَرُّ، الرَّزّاقُ، الهادِي، المَوْلى، النَّصِيرُ، الأعْلى، الأكْبَرُ، الوَهّابُ الجَوادُ، الوَفِيُّ، الواسِعُ، الخَلّاقُ، الوِتْرُ."» [Translator's note: the names are left in Arabic as quoted; the more important ones are explained by the author below.]
It has come in the exegesis that the greatest name of Allah is "اَللَّهُ". Sībawayh said: I asked al-Khalīl about this name, and he said: its origin is "إلَهٌ"; the alif and lām were brought in as a substitute for the hamza. On another occasion he said: its origin is "لاهٌ", and the alif and lām were brought in as an inseparable part.
As for "اَلرَّحْمَنُ الرَّحِيمُ": al-Raḥmān is a name of Allah exclusively; "رَحْمَنُ" is not said of anyone other than Allah. Its meaning is: the One who goes to the utmost in mercy, the Most Merciful of the merciful. "فَعْلانُ" is one of the intensive patterns (bināʾ al-mubālagha): you say of one who is very full "مَلْآنُ", and of one who is very sated "شَبْعانُ". "اَلرَّحِيمُ" is the active participle (ism al-fāʿil) of "رَحِمَ": he is raḥīm; and it too is intensive.
"اَلْأحَدُ": its origin is "اَلْوَحَدُ", in the sense of "اَلْواحِدُ" (the One); He is the One like whom there is nothing.
"اَلصَّمَدُ": the Lord to whom everything turns (ṣamada), that is, makes Him its goal; and the interpretation of everything's turning to Allah is that in everything there is the trace of Allah's workmanship.
"اَلسَّلامُ": the One from whose injustice creation is safe. We have already explained "اَلْمُؤْمِنُ المُهَيْمِنُ", and we have explained "اَلْجَبّارُ المُتَكَبِّرُ".
"اَلْبارِئُ": the Creator; you say "بَرَأ اللَّهُ الخَلْقَ، يَبْرَؤُهُمْ", that is, He created them.
"اَلْقَيُّومُ": the One who goes to the utmost in sustaining everything He has created and everything He has willed.
"اَلْوَلِيُّ": the One who takes charge of the believers; al-Laṭīf to creation in ways they do not know and are not able (to grasp). [Translator's note: "اللَّطِيفُ لِلْخَلْقِ" may be a separate entry for the name al-Laṭīf, "the Subtly Kind"; the text joins it without a conjunction.]
"اَلْوَدُودُ": the Loving, intense in love.
"اَلشَّكُورُ": the One with whom good returns.
"اَلظّاهِرُ الباطِنُ": the One who knows what is manifest and what is hidden.
"اَلْمُبْدِئُ": the One who began everything from nothing. "اَلْبَدِيعُ": the One who originated creation without a prior model.
"اَلْقُدُّوسُ": it has also been transmitted as "اَلقَدُّوسُ", with fatḥa on the qāf. It has come in the exegesis that it means the Blessed; from that comes "أرْضٌ مُقَدَّسَةٌ" (a holy land), that is, blessed. It has also been said: the Pure.
"اَلْمُذْرِئُ", with hamza: the One who brought forth (dharaʾa) creation, that is, created them. [Translator's note: the list above has "الذّارِئُ".]
"اَلْفاصِلُ": the One who separates truth from falsehood.
"اَلْغَفُورُ": the One who forgives sins. The interpretation of "اَلْغُفْرانُ" in the language is covering over a thing; from that comes "اَلْمِغْفَرُ" (the helmet), that with which the head is covered.
"اَلْمَجِيدُ": the One of beautiful deeds. "اَلشَّهِيدُ": the One from whom nothing is absent. "اَلرَّبُّ": the Owner of everything. "اَلصَّفُوحُ": the One who passes over sins and overlooks them (yaṣfaḥu ʿanhā). "اَلْحَنّانُ": the One of mercy and compassion. "اَلْمَنّانُ": the One who bestows abundant favours on His servants through manifest blessings. "اَلْفَتّاحُ": the Judge. "اَلدَّيّانُ": the Requiter. "اَلرَّقِيبُ": the Guardian, from whom nothing is absent. "اَلْمَتِينُ": the One of intense strength over His affair. "اَلْوَكِيلُ": the One entrusted with sustaining all that He has created. "اَلزَّكِيُّ": the One abundant in good. "اَلسُّبُّوحُ": the One who is clear of every secret [Translator's note: so in the text (الَّذِي بَيِّنٌ عَنْ كُلِّ سِرٍّ); the expected sense of subbūḥ is "the One free (barīʾ) of every evil"]. "اَلْحَلِيمُ": the One who does not hasten punishment; so "اَلْحِلْمُ" on this account is the postponement of punishment.
